question: download_max_forks = 2 was set from a download-only probe over WiFi and recorded as 'a saturated link'. The machine is now wired. Does more concurrency help, and what does GenBank-scale fetching actually cost?
answer: Throughput is LINK-limited, not concurrency-limited. From 2 to 12 forks the bandwidth moves 22.4 -> 24.7 MB/s, a 10% gain for 6x the concurrency, and batches start failing at 8. At 16 it collapses to 6.6 MB/s with 5 of 6 batches lost. So the old conclusion -- more forks gain nothing -- was right; the rate was not. Set to 4, the fastest level with zero failures.
design: The COMBINED fetch+screen stage, which is what FETCH_RENAME_SCREEN does: `datasets download --include gbff --assembly-source GenBank --exclude-atypical`, unzip, then pepm_prescreen.py. A download-only probe overstates throughput because the screen runs inline before the next batch starts. 6 batches of 25 per fork level, each level on its own disjoint slice of 4,000 cold GenBank accessions excluded from the RefSeq run's accession list, so nothing is served warm.

measured.columns: forks, genomes retrieved, wall_s, genomes/min, MB, MB/s, failed batches

read_MB_per_s_not_genomes_per_min: Each level drew a different slice and genome size varies 2.4-16 MB across them, so genomes/min mostly reports slice composition: forks=4 looks 1.8x faster than forks=2 on genomes/min while being 3% faster on bandwidth. MB/s is slice-independent and is the number to compare.

what_changed_versus_the_old_probe.old: 33.5 MB/s, 159 genomes/min, peaked at forks=2, download only, over WiFi (2026-09-23)
what_changed_versus_the_old_probe.new: 22-25 MB/s across forks 2-12, fetch+screen combined, wired (2026-10-08)
what_changed_versus_the_old_probe.not_a_regression: The two are not comparable: this one carries the pepM screen inline, which the old one did not. The comparison that matters is against what the RefSeq run actually ACHIEVED -- 70.4 genomes/min sustained over 43 h, implying ~4.7 MB/s. Wired at the same forks=2 is ~5x that.

genbank_projection.basis: 3.38 MB/genome, from the two zero-failure levels only (298 genomes, 1,008 MB)
genbank_projection.so: wired turns the fetch+screen stage from ~11 days into ~2.3 days, and that improvement comes from the link, not from the fork setting
genbank_projection.caveat: The probe drew --assembly-level complete accessions, which biases toward larger, better-assembled genomes than GenBank as a whole. Treat 55 h as an estimate with the sampling bias unmeasured, not as a measurement.

failures: 0 at forks 2 and 4, 1 at 8 and 12, 5 of 6 at 16. The probe has no retry logic; the real process retries a bad batch three times inline and then falls back to one accession at a time, so in production these cost wall-clock rather than genomes. The trend is still a reason not to raise the setting.
